title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named campus spaces with documented uses for studying, gathering, recreation, orientation, dining and exploring university history.

cards.title: Spread Out Beyond the Library’s Main Floor
cards.subtitle: Collaboration space, reservable study rooms and individual carrels
cards.notes: Start group work on the collaborative main floor; move to a reservable room or an individual carrel when the assignment needs more focus.
cards.short_summary: One building supports collaborative projects, scheduled group sessions and quieter solo study.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata states that Gabriele Library has main-floor collaboration space, reservable group study rooms and individual study carrels.
cards.access_notes: Current students use an Immaculata ID as their library card; room reservations and building access may follow library rules.

cards.title: Use the Student Center as a Multi-Activity Base
cards.subtitle: Lounging, games, exercise, dining and club programming under one roof
cards.notes: Meet by the fireplace, use the game room or exercise stations, and check the multipurpose-room calendar before planning a group session.
cards.short_summary: A three-story student hub combines informal seating with recreation and programmable gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes the IHM Student Center as open to graduate, undergraduate, resident and commuter students, with lounges, games, exercise stations, dining and a multipurpose room.
cards.access_notes: Intended for Immaculata students; individual facilities or scheduled programs may have separate operating rules.

cards.title: Take the Group Outside on Back Campus
cards.subtitle: The campus green used for meals, lawn games and major student gatherings
cards.notes: Bring a picnic or outdoor-study setup when the weather works, but check the campus calendar because orientation and student events use the lawn.
cards.short_summary: The large green shifts easily between casual outdoor time and organized campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata identifies Back Campus as green space for picnics, frisbee and outdoor study, and its 2026 orientation schedule places meals, lawn games and the Welcome Back Bash there.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor availability is weather-dependent and may be limited while scheduled university events are underway.

cards.title: Find the Event Lawn Inside the Academic Core
cards.subtitle: A named quad framed by five academic and campus buildings
cards.notes: Use the quad as a meetup point between nearby buildings, and look for scheduled fairs or outdoor programs before claiming space for a group.
cards.short_summary: This centrally framed lawn doubles as a practical rendezvous point and an official event site.
cards.evidence_claim: The university defines Loyola Quad as the area between Alumnae Hall, Faculty Center, Good Counsel, Loyola Hall and Parsons Science Pavilion and says it is used for events.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access may be affected by weather, classes in surrounding buildings or scheduled campus events.

cards.title: Meet Where New Students Learn the Campus Rhythm
cards.subtitle: Villa Maria Hall’s first-floor orientation and gathering landmark
cards.notes: Use the first-floor Rotunda as a clear meetup landmark; during move-in or orientation, follow posted traffic and program directions.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable interior landmark serves check-in, ceremonies and transition points during orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata’s 2026 orientation schedule names the first-floor Villa Maria Rotunda for commuter check-in and the orientation closing ceremony.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Villa Maria Hall; access may be managed during move-in, orientation and other scheduled functions.

cards.title: Watch the Great Hall Change Jobs by the Hour
cards.subtitle: A formal hall used for fairs, games, check-in and student discussions
cards.notes: Check the event schedule before heading over: the room can host anything from orientation check-in to a fair, roundtable or evening games.
cards.short_summary: The same formal room becomes an administrative checkpoint, activity floor or campus conversation space.
cards.evidence_claim: Current university schedules place transfer check-in, a University Life Fair and a student roundtable in the Great Hall, while new-student orientation uses it for games and move-in.
cards.access_notes: The Great Hall is an event venue rather than an unrestricted lounge; enter when your program or a publicized event permits.

cards.title: Look Beyond Performances at Alumnae Hall Theater
cards.subtitle: A shared auditorium for films, presentations and campus ceremonies
cards.notes: Scan the campus schedule for films, performances and student presentations; seating access depends on the specific program using the theater.
cards.short_summary: The campus theater supports both performing arts and large shared student sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata’s 2026 orientation schedule places its welcome, involvement panel, student presentations and a Mighty Macs movie in Alumnae Hall Theater.
cards.access_notes: Entry is tied to scheduled performances, presentations and university programs; ticketing or registration may vary by event.

cards.title: Pair a Library Stop With ImmacuLatté
cards.subtitle: The café located on Gabriele Library’s main floor
cards.notes: Use the café as a convenient meeting marker inside the library, then carry work to an appropriate study area after ordering and checking posted hours.
cards.short_summary: A named campus café anchors the library’s main floor near academic and career-support services.
cards.evidence_claim: The university places ImmacuLatté Café on Gabriele Library’s main floor and identifies it as an on-campus dining location offering drinks and prepared food.
cards.access_notes: Service hours vary with the academic calendar; the university announced that the café closed for summer after May 8, 2026.

cards.title: Keep Residence-Hall Study Separate From the Lounge
cards.subtitle: A dedicated study room inside Gillet Hall
cards.notes: If you live in Gillet, use the dedicated room when lounge activity is distracting; respect residence access controls and community quiet rules.
cards.short_summary: Gillet distinguishes focused academic space from its general community lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata’s residential-community page states that Gillet Hall includes both a community lounge and a dedicated study room.
cards.access_notes: Gillet Hall is a secured residence hall with ID-swipe access; use is limited to residents and authorized guests.

cards.title: Ask for the Campus Story Behind the Campus
cards.subtitle: Immaculata University Archives on Gabriele Library’s second floor
cards.notes: Bring a focused research question, visit during posted business hours or arrange an appointment, and ask staff which archival materials fit your topic.
cards.short_summary: The Heritage Room turns institutional records into a research resource for students and other scholars.
cards.evidence_claim: Immaculata states that its Archives are in the Heritage Room on Gabriele Library’s second floor and support teaching, research and scholarship.
cards.access_notes: Visits may be arranged by appointment or made during business hours; the university says the office is usually open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.
